title: Subtracting Fractions with Unlike Denominators
short: Rename to like pieces, then subtract.

blocks.html: Subtracting works just like adding unlike fractions: first make the pieces the same size, then take some away.
Rename the fractions with a common denominator, then subtract the numerators. Keep the denominator. Check by adding your answer back.

You can take 2 twelfths from 9 twelfths because they are the same kind of piece. You cannot take a third straight out of three fourths, since thirds do not line up with fourths. Renamed as twelfths, $\frac{3}{4} - \frac{1}{3}$ is $\frac{9}{12} - \frac{4}{12}$, and the answer is the 5 twelfths left over.

blocks.name: fractionbar
blocks.cap: Drag the guide to the end of the shorter shading. The difference between the bars is the answer to $\frac{3}{4} - \frac{1}{3}$.

blocks.html: Subtracting tops and bottoms: $\frac{3}{4} - \frac{1}{3} = \frac{2}{1} = 2$. Taking something away from less than 1 cannot give 2. Always rename first, and check by adding back.
